body.statement: Let \(B^{(k)}\) contain \(k\) blocks of size two and \(k\) blocks of size four, so \(n=6k\). Then the two strata have \((w_l,q_l)=(1/(3k),1/4)\) and \((2/(3k),1/16)\), respectively, \(S=68/(9k)\), and \(M=32/(3k)\). For fixed \(\alpha\), the dominance ratio is \(32\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}/\sqrt{68k}\to0\), and \(\mathrm{thm{:}no\text{-}dominance\text{-}frontier}\) predicts minimax length of order \(\sqrt{68\log(1/\alpha)/(9k)}\). No common block size \(r\) can reproduce both reveal probabilities \(1/4\) and \(1/16\) or the two water-filling breakpoint values.
body.justification: This concrete triangular array makes the heterogeneous theorem refutable through exact constants and a nondegenerate two-scale exposure structure.
body.gap: The inherited equal-block formula collapses all blocks to one reveal probability and one cap threshold, so it cannot deliver this two-stratum prediction.
body.consumer: A simulation study and the package diagnostic can check the predicted \(k^{-1/2}\) confidence-length curve separately within the two exposure strata.
